title: Surface air temperature for August 2026
bodyText: August 2026 was the warmest August globally , with an average surface air temperature of 16.96°C, 0.85°C above the 1991-2020 average for the month, surpassing the previous joint records set in August 2023 and August 2024. Both had an average temperature of 16.82°C, or 0.71°C above average.

title: Sea ice cover for August 2026
bodyText: Arctic sea ice extent averaged 6.1 million km² in August 2026 , 0.6 million km² or 9.2% below the 1991–2020 average for August . This was the 12th-lowest August extent in the 48-year satellite record, a less notable ranking than the sixth-lowest in July , reflecting a slowing of the seasonal decline in sea ice extent during August.

title: Precipitation, relative humidity, soil moisture and river flow for August 2026
originalTitle: Precipitation, relative humidity, soil moisture and river flow for August 2026
bodyText: Exceptionally low flows affected many of Europe's major rivers, particularly the Rhine, Danube and rivers across eastern Europe. During the month, record-low levels were also reported for several individual locations along parts of the Rhine, Danube, Loire, Po , Vistula and Elbe , as well as record-low inflows to the Dniester reservoir.

title: August 2026 was joint hottest month ever recorded globally
originalTitle: August 2026 was joint hottest month ever recorded globally
bodyText: August 2026 was the joint hottest month ever recorded around the world. Global temperatures reached 1.65C above preindustrial levels, scientists said on Thursday, amid warnings of further heating. Last month tied with July 2023 for the hottest on record, according to the EU’s Copernicus Climate Change Service.

title: Analysis: ‘Super El Niño’ breaks ‘remarkable’ all-time record
originalTitle: Analysis: ‘Super El Niño’ breaks ‘remarkable’ all-time record
bodyText: As of 21 September, the daily anomaly in the Niño 3.4 region stands at 3.11C, surpassing the previous record of 3.08C. Some scientists, using a different baseline for calculating the anomaly, called the new record a few days before. Either way, this is remarkable, in part because of how early in the calendar year it is occurring.

title: Why is this monster El Niño so strong?
originalTitle: Why is this monster El Niño so strong?
bodyText: Mind-blowing. Unprecedented. Off the charts. Jaw-dropping. Godzilla-level. Superlatives have been flying about the current El Niño climate pattern, which is already the strongest on record months before it is expected to peak – and unusually, they are coming from scientists, rather than the media.

title: ‘Concerning’ low sea ice persists as Antarctic hits third-lowest winter peak
originalTitle: ‘Concerning’ low sea ice persists as Antarctic hits third-lowest winter peak
bodyText: Antarctic sea ice has recorded its third-smallest winter peak extent since satellite records began 48 years ago, new data reveals. Provisional data from the US National Snow and Ice Data Center (NSIDC) shows that Antarctic sea ice hit its annual winter peak on 14 September, with an extent of 17.59m square kilometres (km2).

title: Faster-flowing glaciers fuel decades of polar ice loss
originalTitle: Faster-flowing glaciers fuel decades of polar ice loss
bodyText: The longest satellite data record of ice-sheet change ever assembled has revealed that Greenland and Antarctica have lost a staggering 11 trillion tonnes of ice since the 1970s, driving global sea level up by more than three centimetres.

title: Earlier and faster heatwave onset on land under a warming climate
originalTitle: Earlier and faster heatwave onset on land under a warming climate
bodyText: Heatwaves threaten ecosystems and societies. Previous studies have examined their frequency, intensity and duration, whereas long-term changes in heatwave timing—including onset, ending and season length—remain poorly understood, limiting our ability to anticipate heat-related risks. Here we analyse global changes in these metrics and onset-speed type from 1979 to 2023.

title: Despite a drop in deforestation in 2025, forest losses pile up in the Mekong
originalTitle: Despite a drop in deforestation in 2025, forest losses pile up in the Mekong
bodyText: Over the course of 2025, Cambodia, Laos, Myanmar, Thailand and Vietnam lost a combined 746,168 hectares of tree cover (1.8 million acres), including more than 154,000 hectares (380,000 acres) of primary forest, according to Mongabay’s analysis of data published by the University of Maryland and Global Nature Watch.

title: Analysis: Global fossil-fuel emissions set to fall in 2026 amid Hormuz crisis
originalTitle: Analysis: Global fossil-fuel emissions set to fall in 2026 amid Hormuz crisis
bodyText: Global fossil-fuel emissions are set to fall by around 0.5% in 2026 amid the fallout from the Hormuz crisis, according to Carbon Brief analysis. The US-Iran war has severely disrupted trade through the strait of Hormuz, causing a spike in oil and gas prices that continues to ripple around the global economy.

title: 3rd C3S NCP Expert Workshop
bodyText: The 3 rd C3S National Collaboration Programme (NCP) Expert Workshop took place online on 18 June 2026, from 15:00 to 17:00 CEST. The workshop provided an overview of upcoming Copernicus Climate Change Service (C3S) data and products relevant to agriculture.

title: Surface air temperature maps
bodyText: We produce surface air temperature maps as a data product, but you can also view the data directly. From April 2019 onward, the temperature summaries are based on ERA5. You can read more on the ' Climate Bulletin - About the data page '.
